problems.explain: The common denominator is (x + 1)(x + 5), the two denominators multiplied, since they share no factor. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times (x + 5), the second top times (x + 1). Combine the numerators: (x + 5) + (x + 1) = 2x + 6. So (2x + 6)/((x + 1)(x + 5)).

The common denominator is (x + 1)(x + 3), the two denominators multiplied, since they share no factor. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times (x + 3), the second top times (x + 1). Combine the numerators: (x + 3) + 2(x + 1) = 3x + 5. So (3x + 5)/((x + 1)(x + 3)).

The common denominator is (x + 1)(x − 3), the two denominators multiplied, since they share no factor. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times (x − 3), the second top times (x + 1). Combine the numerators: (x − 3) + 2(x + 1) = 3x − 1. So (3x − 1)/((x + 1)(x − 3)).

The common denominator is (x + 1)(x − 2), the two denominators multiplied, since they share no factor. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times (x − 2), the second top times (x + 1). Combine the numerators, the minus taking away all of the second: (x − 2) − (x + 1) = −3. So −3/((x + 1)(x − 2)).

The common denominator is (x + 2)(x − 4), the two denominators multiplied, since they share no factor. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times (x − 4), the second top times (x + 2). Combine the numerators: (x − 4) + (x + 2) = 2x − 2. So (2x − 2)/((x + 2)(x − 4)).

The common denominator is x(x + 2), the two denominators multiplied, since they share no factor. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times x, the second top times (x + 2). Combine the numerators: x + 4(x + 2) = 5x + 8. So (5x + 8)/(x(x + 2)).

The common denominator is (x + 2)(x + 4), the two denominators multiplied, since they share no factor. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times (x + 4), the second top times (x + 2). Combine the numerators, the minus taking away all of the second: (x + 4) − 4(x + 2) = −3x − 4. So (−3x − 4)/((x + 2)(x + 4)).

Factor the denominators: x² + 5x + 6 = (x + 3)(x + 2). The common denominator is (x + 3)(x + 2): the factor both denominators have is needed only once, so it is less than their product. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times (x + 2), the second is over it already. Combine the numerators: (x + 2) + 6 = x + 8. So (x + 8)/((x + 3)(x + 2)).

The common denominator is (x + 3)(x − 5), the two denominators multiplied, since they share no factor. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times (x − 5), the second top times (x + 3). Combine the numerators, the minus taking away all of the second: (x − 5) − 5(x + 3) = −4x − 20. So (−4x − 20)/((x + 3)(x − 5)).

The common denominator is (x + 4)(x − 3), the two denominators multiplied, since they share no factor. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times (x − 3), the second top times (x + 4). Combine the numerators: (x − 3) + 5(x + 4) = 6x + 17. So (6x + 17)/((x + 4)(x − 3)).

Combine the numerators, the minus taking away all of the second: (x + 1) − (x + 4) = −3. So −3/((x + 4)(x + 1)).

Combine the numerators, the minus taking away all of the second: (x − 3) − (x + 4) = −7. So −7/((x + 4)(x − 3)).

The common denominator is x(x + 3), the two denominators multiplied, since they share no factor. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times (x + 3), the second top times x. Combine the numerators, the minus taking away all of the second: (x + 3) − 4x = −3x + 3. So (−3x + 3)/(x(x + 3)).

Factor the denominators: x² + 2x − 3 = (x + 3)(x − 1) and x² − 9 = (x + 3)(x − 3). The common denominator is (x + 3)(x − 1)(x − 3): the factor both denominators have is needed only once, so it is less than their product. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times (x − 3), the second top times (x − 1). Combine the numerators, the minus taking away all of the second: (x − 3) − 5(x − 1) = −4x + 2. So (−4x + 2)/((x + 3)(x − 1)(x − 3)).

Factor the denominators: x² + 2x − 8 = (x + 4)(x − 2) and x² − 16 = (x + 4)(x − 4). So −x/((x + 4)(x − 2)(x − 4)).

Factor the denominators: x² + 2x = (x + 2)x and x² − 4 = (x + 2)(x − 2). The common denominator is x(x + 2)(x − 2): the factor both denominators have is needed only once, so it is less than their product. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times (x − 2), the second top times x. Combine the numerators: (x − 2) + 6x = 7x − 2. So (7x − 2)/(x(x + 2)(x − 2)).

Multiply each fraction up to it: the first is over it already, the second top times (x − 3). Combine the numerators: 1 + 2(x − 3) = 2x − 5. So (2x − 5)/((x + 6)(x − 3)).

Multiply each fraction up to it: the first is over it already, the second top times (x − 1). Combine the numerators: 1 + x(x − 1) = x² − x + 1. So (x² − x + 1)/((x + 4)(x − 1)).

Factor the denominators: x² + 3x − 4 = (x + 4)(x − 1) and x² + 7x + 12 = (x + 4)(x + 3). The common denominator is (x + 4)(x − 1)(x + 3): the factor both denominators have is needed only once, so it is less than their product. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times (x + 3), the second top times (x − 1). Combine the numerators, the minus taking away all of the second: (x + 3) − 4(x − 1) = −3x + 7. So (−3x + 7)/((x + 4)(x − 1)(x + 3)).

The common denominator is (x + 6)(x − 2)(x − 4): the factor both denominators have is needed only once, so it is less than their product. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times (x − 4), the second top times (x − 2). Combine the numerators: (x − 4) + 2(x − 2) = 3x − 8. So (3x − 8)/((x + 6)(x − 2)(x − 4)).

Multiply each fraction up to it: the first is over it already, the second top times (x + 4). Combine the numerators: 1 + 3(x + 4) = 3x + 13. So (3x + 13)/((x + 1)(x + 4)).

Factor the denominators: x² + 5x = (x + 5)x and x² − x − 30 = (x + 5)(x − 6). The common denominator is x(x + 5)(x − 6): the factor both denominators have is needed only once, so it is less than their product. Multiply each fraction up to it: the first top times (x − 6), the second top times x. Combine the numerators: (x − 6) + 2x = 3x − 6. So (3x − 6)/(x(x + 5)(x − 6)).
